title: Bugsee WebView Bridge Protocol v1
description: The versioned JSON envelope crossing the WebView boundary (docs/design/webview-bridge.md §6). JS->native kinds: hello | entry | batch | report | secure | bye. native->JS kind: control. Every message carries `b` (protocol version). `p` is the per-kind payload INLINE as a JSON value (an object for entry/report, an array for secure) — the JS host splices the already-serialized payload in verbatim (serialize once), so native does exactly ONE JSON.parse of the whole message (no nested/second parse). Receivers MUST ignore unknown fields/kinds (forward-compatible); this schema validates that the SDK EMITS well-formed messages (hence additionalProperties:false on the emitter side).

fileType.description: The capture stream a record belongs to (native routes by it).

hello.description: JS->native: the opening handshake declaring the SDK version, capabilities, and session.

n.description: The capture nonce (D-A11). Native mints it, interpolates it into the bundle it injects, and DROPS any inbound message that does not carry it — `BugseeBridge.post` is reachable from every frame, so this is the only thing distinguishing the SDK's traffic from a page script's. Optional on the wire so a host that mints no nonce still validates; a native receiver that mints one MUST require it.

tok.description: SUPERSEDED by D-A10 — a receiver MUST NOT store or echo this. It was minted by the JS SDK and published here so native could learn it, which authenticated nobody: `hello` arrives on the same @JavascriptInterface any frame can post to, so native cannot tell this token from one a page script minted. That is why the channel had to start open and wait to latch, and why a script could stop capture inside that window. Native mints its OWN secret instead and delivers it inside the bundle it injects (see `control.tok`). The field stays on the wire only so an older SDK still validates.

entry.description: JS->native: one streamed capture entry. `p` is the entry's payload INLINE (a {timestamp,data} object), keyed by `t`.

control.description: native->JS: the handshake reply + ongoing control commands.

tok.description: The control secret NATIVE minted (D-A10) — 128 bits of CSPRNG, interpolated into the bundle native injects as `BugseeWebView.launch(token,{controlNonce})`, so it reaches the SDK by a route the page never observes. Required on EVERY control message, from the first: the SDK rejects anything else with no open period and no latch to race. It must NOT be derived from `hello.tok`, which any page script can mint. It must also differ from the capture nonce `n`: that one necessarily travels the wire, so sharing them would let a script tapping the outgoing stream send commands.

secureArea.description: One masked rect inside a `secure` message's `p` payload (DOCUMENT-absolute coordinates).
